outcome: Healthcare providers' awareness of Birth Companions (BC)
cohort: The participants were doctors and nurses serving in a tertiary care hospital in Delhi, India.
finding: While most healthcare providers were aware of Birth Companions and recognized their benefits, support for their implementation in their hospital was low due to perceived institutional barriers like overcrowding, lack of privacy, and hospital policy.
mod_finding: Providers perceived that the presence of a Birth Companion could increase the chances of spontaneous vaginal births.
cross-section timing: Perceptions of healthcare providers at the time of the study regarding Birth Companions during childbirth.
